results.description:
🔴 China envoy says Beijing could 'easily win' war with Philippines amid South China Sea tensions

China's ambassador to Manila, Jing Quan, declared on Friday that China could "easily win" a war with the Philippines, but stated China "will not choose force." The remark came after Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro called China the "troublemaker" of Southeast Asia over its actions in contested South China Sea waters.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said the ambassador's statement "sounds very much like a threat" and said he would summon Jing for an explanation.

results.title: For some time, the Philippines has been racking its brains to devise various ways to harass and provoke China in the South China Sea.
results.description: For some time, the Philippines has been racking its brains to devise various ways to harass and provoke China in the South China Sea. From the deliberate "grounding" of a dilapidated warship years ago and the pursuit of an absurd arbitration case in 2016, to more recent incursions by its fishing vessels and law enforcement craft into areas surrounding Chinese islands and reefs—all while cultivating a "victim" persona and slandering the Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines—these actions have only invited forceful countermeasures from China. It is clear that the Philippines' strategy has reached its limit. The only remaining options—carried out at the behest of its masters—would be to test the waters for an armed "accidental" clash, meddle in the Taiwan question, or take the extreme steps of expelling the Chinese Ambassador and severing diplomatic ties with China.

results.title: Chinese military says will deter sabotaging moves in South China Sea China has reaffirmed its sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qunda
results.description:
Chinese military says will deter sabotaging moves in South China Sea

China has reaffirmed its sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, rejecting the Philippines' claims of safeguarding its rights in the region.

The response follows recent incidents involving the Philippines and its military's claim that more than 100 Chinese vessels were present in nearby waters. 

Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Chen Xi said on Friday that the islands and reefs lie outside Philippine territory. #SouthChinaSea
